title: Dynamic graph query generation (LLM-generated graph queries)
keyFindings: Dynamic graph query generation is the Graph RAG path where an LLM translates a natural-language question into a structured graph query (Cypher/SPARQL) at query time and executes it against a knowledge graph — the generated query doubles as the explainability trace, directly answering the source talk's 'vectors don't capture relationship data' and 'vector similarity != relevance' failures.

Astrographer's data model is already a knowledge graph (fact/reference/embed nodes and edges, astrographer.md §4.2), so an LLM-generated graph query over the reference→fact graph is a natural, graph-native fit for relationship-aware and multi-hop retrieval; it is NOT in the spec (§4.3.2 pins a string query) and is a proposed spec change.

The technique is gated on a graph-query substrate (a Cypher/SPARQL executor) over Provident graphs, which the suite does not yet have — the dominant cost/benefit consideration and the reason it is SHOULD, not MUST.

Zodiac's graph mode (zodiac.md §4.3.2) already returns a pre-graphed subgraph; a generated graph query adds precision (retrieve only the relevant subgraph) rather than capability, so it is lower priority than Astrographer's.

The engine boundary (Incanter) is the correct home for query-time graph retrieval, mirroring GAP-1 (multi-query belongs inside Incanter, docs/defects.md) — a handoff candidate, not a this-repo change.

D2 (local LLM + local graph) and D4 (a retrieval-mode change, not a security carve-out) are both satisfied; the technique should land after the MUST/SHOULD retrieval foundation (reranking, multi-query, hybrid, compression) ships, consistent with the sibling graph-rag-astrographer report's PARKED-until-foundation note.
summary: Dynamic graph query generation is a high-value, graph-native retrieval technique in which an LLM writes a structured graph query (Cypher/SPARQL) per question and executes it against a knowledge graph, directly expressing relationship-aware and multi-hop retrieval and doubling as an explainability trace. It is a strong fit for Astrographer (whose data model is already a knowledge graph) and a lower-priority fit for Zodiac, but it is gated on a graph-query substrate the suite does not yet have, so it is a SHOULD that lands after the MUST/SHOULD retrieval foundation ships.
